description: Three event types, the bidding process, and the pre-event costs and benefits a host city must weigh up.
content_html:
Types of Major Sporting Event

Not all major sporting events are alike. Before examining what it takes to host one, it is important to understand the three categories that appear on the specification. Getting these right is a common mark-scoring opportunity — and a common source of lost marks when students muddle the definitions.

Key Fact

The three types of major sporting event are: one-off (held in a host city once in a generation — e.g. the Olympic and Paralympic Games); regular (held repeatedly but in a different city each time — e.g. the UEFA Champions League Final); and regular and recurring (held repeatedly at the same venue — e.g. Wimbledon or the Monaco Grand Prix).

Students frequently swap the categories. Here is the clearest way to remember them: One-off — the same city is unlikely to host again in your lifetime (Paris last hosted the summer Olympics in 1900; it returned in 2024 after 100 years). Regular — the event happens every year or two years, but in a different city: the Champions League Final has been held in Madrid, Istanbul, Paris and Wembley in recent seasons. Regular and recurring — same event, same location, every year: Wimbledon at the All England Club, the British Grand Prix at Silverstone. Always anchor each category to its named spec example in an exam answer.

The Nature of Participants and Spectators

Major events draw participants and spectators from very different backgrounds depending on their type. A one-off event like the Olympics attracts athletes from every nation on Earth and millions of global tourists — the 2024 Paris Games sold over 9 million tickets. A regular event like the Champions League Final has a smaller but intensely passionate fanbase that travels with the finalists. A regular and recurring event like Wimbledon draws a stable, often high-income, domestic and international audience to its permanent home in south London every June and July.

Why Host a Major Event? The Bidding Process

Cities and nations bid to host major events. For the Olympic Games, the International Olympic Committee (IOC) assesses bids from candidate cities. For the FIFA World Cup, FIFA makes the award to a national federation. Bidding requires submitting a detailed proposal covering: stadium and venue capacity, athlete village accommodation, transport links, security plans, broadcasting infrastructure, accommodation for spectators, and plans for what happens to facilities after the event — the legacy plan.

The bidding process is expensive in itself. Major bid campaigns can cost tens of millions of pounds before a single ticket is sold. Cities that lose their bid have spent that money for nothing, which is why many cities are now reluctant to enter the race. Several candidate cities withdrew from the 2024 Olympic bid before Paris and Los Angeles were selected for 2024 and 2028 respectively — concerns about cost and public opposition were the main reasons cited.

Key Fact

A successful Olympic or World Cup bid must address: venue and infrastructure; transport; security; accommodation; legacy planning; and financial viability. The IOC (for the Olympics) or FIFA (for the World Cup) evaluates bids against these criteria before awarding the event.

Pre-Event Positives

Even before the opening ceremony, hosting a major event delivers tangible benefits. Infrastructure development begins years in advance: new roads, rail lines, airports, and broadband networks are built or upgraded to meet event requirements. These improvements benefit local residents long after the event ends. Construction employment surges as stadiums, athlete villages, and media centres are built — providing thousands of jobs in an often short space of time.

Commercial investment flows into the host city as businesses respond to the opportunity of an arriving global audience. Hotels, restaurants and retail all benefit from advance bookings. The host nation also gains international profile and prestige — the Paris 2024 Games showcased France on the world stage, with the opening ceremony along the Seine attracting a global television audience estimated at 1.5 billion viewers. Tourism in the months and years following the event can also increase, as the host city gains new visibility.

Not everyone is delighted when their city wins a major event bid. Cost overruns are almost universal in Olympic host cities: the Paris 2024 Games budget grew from an initial estimate of around 3.6 billion euros to approximately 8.8 billion euros by the time the Games opened. Taxpayers bear most of this gap. Displacement is another concern: building venues and athlete villages often requires demolishing housing in less affluent areas, with residents relocated — sometimes with inadequate compensation. Local communities may face years of construction noise, disrupted roads and reduced access to their own neighbourhood. Political opposition can also mobilise: residents may vote or campaign against the event, causing friction between government ambitions and public sentiment.
exam_tip_html: This topic uses ‘describe’ and ‘explain’ command words frequently. When asked to describe an event type, always give the definition and a named example — the mark scheme almost always requires both. For a ‘discuss’ or ‘evaluate’ question on hosting decisions, remember to cover pre-event impacts (positive and negative) separately from during-event and post-event legacy impacts — mixing them up suggests you have not structured your answer carefully. When you name a cost figure (such as the Paris 2024 budget), make sure it is attached to a clear positive or negative point rather than just a statistic floating in your answer.
conclusion_html:
Key Takeaways

  • Major sporting events fall into three types: one-off (e.g. Olympics, one city per generation), regular (e.g. Champions League Final, different city each time), and regular and recurring (e.g. Wimbledon, same venue each year).
  • Bidding requires covering venues, transport, security, accommodation, finance and legacy. The IOC awards the Olympics; FIFA awards the World Cup. Bids are expensive even for losing cities.
  • Pre-event positives include infrastructure investment, construction jobs, commercial activity and international profile. Negatives include budget overruns, community displacement and political opposition.

practice_questions.text:
Which one of the following is an example of a 'regular and recurring' major sporting event?
A) The FIFA World Cup
B) The UEFA Champions League Final
C) The Summer Olympic Games
D) Wimbledon
practice_questions.marks:
D) Wimbledon [1 mark]
(Wimbledon is held every year at the same venue — the All England Club. The World Cup and Champions League Final are 'regular' events held in different locations. The Olympics is a 'one-off' event.)

practice_questions.text: State two positive impacts for a host city in the period before a major sporting event takes place.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per distinct positive (maximum 2 marks). Acceptable answers:
- Infrastructure development (new roads, rail, airports)
- Increased construction employment / job creation
- Commercial investment / business growth
- International profile / media attention raised pre-event
- Tourism bookings increase in advance of the event
- Urban regeneration of the host area
Do not award a second mark for the same point restated (e.g. 'jobs' and 'more workers employed' = 1 mark only).

practice_questions.text: Explain the difference between a 'one-off' and a 'regular' major sporting event. Give one example of each.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark for correct definition of one-off (held in a host city once in a generation / same city very unlikely to host again for many decades). Award 1 mark for correct definition of regular (held repeatedly in different cities each time). Award 1 mark for a correct named example of each:
- One-off: Olympic / Paralympic Games, FIFA World Cup, Commonwealth Games
- Regular: UEFA Champions League Final, World Athletics Championships, Rugby World Cup
Do not award for 'Wimbledon' as a regular example — it is regular and recurring.

practice_questions.text: Describe two reasons why a city government might have concerns about bidding for the right to host the Summer Olympics. Use examples to support your answer.
practice_questions.marks:
Award up to 4 marks. Credit two distinct concerns with development:
- Cost overruns: Olympic budgets almost always exceed initial estimates — Paris 2024 grew from ~3.6bn to ~8.8bn euros. Taxpayers fund the gap.
- Displacement and community disruption: building venues requires relocating residents, often from lower-income areas, who may receive inadequate compensation.
- Political opposition: public may resist via protest or referendum, causing reputational and governance problems for the host government.
- Bid cost with no guarantee: a bid campaign alone costs tens of millions; a losing city gets nothing back.
A named example is required for the top marks. An answer without any named example is capped at 2 marks.

practice_questions.text:
Thornfield City Council is considering bidding for the right to host a major international athletics championship. Some councillors are in favour; others are opposed.

Discuss the pre-event advantages and disadvantages a host city like Thornfield would need to consider before submitting its bid.
practice_questions.marks:
Mastering (5-6 marks): Balanced discussion addressing at least two distinct pre-event advantages and two distinct disadvantages. Points are developed and interact with each other (e.g. infrastructure benefit has to be weighed against cost of building it). Applied context used. Points are not just listed but linked into a reasoned argument.

Secure (3-4 marks): At least two valid points on each side with some development. Limited interaction between points. May not address all key areas.

Developing (2 marks): Two or more valid points identified but little development. One-sided or near-one-sided.

Emerging (1 mark): A single valid pre-event factor identified, with no development.

Credit: advantages — infrastructure (roads/rail/broadband), construction jobs, commercial investment, tourism bookings, raised national/city profile. Disadvantages — bid cost risk, construction cost overruns, displacement of residents, noise/disruption during build phase, political opposition from local community.

practice_questions.text: Identify two organisations that assess bids for major sporting events. For each organisation, name the event they award.
practice_questions.marks:
Award 1 mark per correct organisation-event pairing (maximum 2 marks):
- IOC (International Olympic Committee) — awards the Summer and Winter Olympic Games
- FIFA — awards the FIFA World Cup
Also accept: IOC for Paralympic Games (awarded alongside the Olympics to the same host city).
Do not award for naming the organisation alone without its associated event.

knowledge_checks.q: Which type of major sporting event is held in a different host city each time it takes place?
Which organisation assesses and awards the hosting rights for the Summer Olympic Games?
A _____ event, like the Olympics, is hosted by a different city once in a generation and is unlikely to return to the same host for many decades.
Wimbledon is an example of a _____ event because it is held every year at the same venue.
Match each major event to its correct event type.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a 'one-off' major sporting event?
flashcard_questions.a: An event hosted in a city once in a generation — the same city is very unlikely to host again for many decades.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one example of a 'one-off' major sporting event.
flashcard_questions.a: The Summer Olympic and Paralympic Games.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a 'regular' major sporting event?
flashcard_questions.a: An event held repeatedly, but in a different host city each time.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one example of a 'regular' major sporting event.
What is a 'regular and recurring' major sporting event?
flashcard_questions.a: An event held every year at the same venue.

flashcard_questions.q: Give one example of a 'regular and recurring' major sporting event.
flashcard_questions.a: Wimbledon (or the Monaco Grand Prix / British Grand Prix at Silverstone).

flashcard_questions.q: Which body awards the hosting rights for the Olympic Games?
Which body awards the hosting rights for the FIFA World Cup?
Name two pre-event positives of hosting a major sporting event.
flashcard_questions.a: Infrastructure development and increased construction employment.

flashcard_questions.q: What is 'displacement' as a pre-event negative of hosting?
flashcard_questions.a: Residents, often in lower-income areas, are forced to relocate to make way for new venues.

flashcard_questions.q: Paris 2024 budget grew from 3.6bn euros to approximately how much?

glossary_terms.definition: A major sporting event held in a single host city on a once-in-a-generation basis, such as the Olympic or Paralympic Games.
A major sporting event held repeatedly at a different host city each time, such as the UEFA Champions League Final.
A major sporting event held every year at the same venue, such as Wimbledon or the Monaco Grand Prix.
